title: fisc series projection
description: One document internal/project builds as a series per printed row rather than as a graph: the revenue trends and the two ACFR fund-balance schedules. These are the only projections a reader fetches as themselves -- internal/export folds the graph documents into one file per column and copies these through verbatim -- so this schema holds bytes that are served rather than only passed between packages.

metadata.description: THE ENVELOPE AND NO MORE. It carries no fiscal_year, fiscal_year_label, basis or headline, and their absence is the contract rather than an omission: a document of four columns and three bases has no singular year or basis, and publishing them zeroed to keep a familiar shape is the absent-is-not-zero error this project refuses everywhere else. `columns` is what carries them, one entry per printed column.

comparable_group.description: Which columns may be read against each other. A basis is not a comparability claim on its own -- the ACFR's ten audited years are one group and the budget book's actual, revised and adopted columns are three.

counts.description: NO facts_cited HERE. Every point IS a fact, so the gap the graph documents state between facts and facts_cited has nothing to be a gap between.

fund.description: NULL AND NOT ZERO where the row sits under no numbered fund -- the ACFR's fund-balance schedules print a fund's components and an aggregate across funds, never a fund. It is fact.Fact.Fund carried through, and no fund is numbered 0, so zero would be a fund rather than the absence of one. AGENTS.md, "Provenance invariants".

items.description: ONE POINT IS ONE FACT, carrying the provenance the fact carries: which page, which byte, which token. That is what lets a reader of this file check a figure without holding the fact store as well.
